question: How should `/reasoning stream` present live reasoning in the TUI: transient chat output, footer/status text, or history-only disclosure?
rationale: Current main has a producer-side thinking event path, but the issue asks for a user-facing terminal experience and the right placement affects chat history semantics, run-status UI, and privacy expectations.

options.title: Render transient chat thinking
options.body: Show live thinking in the terminal chat stream while preserving the existing opt-in and thinking-off gates, using the chat rendering path as the closest match to existing thinking block support.

options.title: Use footer/status preview
options.body: Show only the latest reasoning snippet in the run-status area, which matches the reporter's later suggestion but requires careful handling so it does not obscure lifecycle state.

options.title: Keep history-only disclosure
options.body: Leave live TUI rendering out of scope and only fix discoverability/docs, accepting that TUI users must inspect reasoning after the run.

recommendation.title: Render transient chat thinking
recommendation.body: Show live thinking in the terminal chat stream while preserving the existing opt-in and thinking-off gates, using the chat rendering path as the closest match to existing thinking block support.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision mostly concerns the `/reasoning` TUI command and thinking UX originally introduced with the visibility feature.
